_schema: Proof-shelf data. Every number rendered on /work/, /work/marcus/, /work/marcus/results/, / and the industry/security pages comes ONLY from here, stamped between BUILD-LOG markers by scripts/build-work.mjs. Never hand-edit a rendered figure. signed_off: true requires the client's written approval on file.

marcus.window_note: Every figure on this page is reconstructable from the tamper-evident audit log — that is the point of having one.

approval.client_sign_off: B:Side Capital — written approval on file
approval.basis: Figures reconciled against the tamper-evident audit log for the measurement window.

scorecard.desc: Staff hours of preparation returned in 90 days — a ~5,000-hour annual run rate, roughly 2.4 full-time people of pure prep work.
Of staff using MARCUS weekly by week six — with no new app, no new login, and no training deck.
Borrower identifiers sent to any outside model. Every prompt and document cleared the privacy filter first. No exceptions, because no bypass exists.
Of consequential actions approved by a person before anything sent, filed, posted, or paid. Zero unapproved actions — verified by the audit log, not asserted.

figures.desc: Uptime since commissioning in August — one planned maintenance window, zero unplanned outages.
Model calls processed entirely on-premises in 90 days. In normal operation, none left the building.
Hardware markup. Bought at cost, in the client's name. That we do not mark it up is the point.
Mid-flight model upgrade, completed in an evening, with zero workflow changes for staff.
Of prompts and attachments cleared the filter before reaching any model. No bypass path exists in the architecture.
Personal identifiers detected and stripped — names, SSNs, account numbers — across ~38,000 documents processed.
Detection recall on the monthly seeded red-team test — measured, not claimed, and improving each cycle.
PII incidents since the filter went live. The number the board actually asks about.
From completed questionnaire to a queryable knowledge base — generated from the intake, not hand-designed.
Process documents ingested, joined with thousands of loan records and a decade of institutional correspondence.
Questions asked by staff by month three — the questions that used to wait for whoever just knows.
Of answers delivered with a citation to the source document or record. The rest say they do not know, and escalate to a person.
From go-live to the first real staff question — no training session had happened yet. None was needed.
Weekly active adoption by week six, across all seven divisions — including the skeptics.
Of all MARCUS interactions happen in Slack — finished work delivered to the channel where the team already works.
Conversations per week by month three — policy lookups, document summaries, and first drafts leading the mix.
Of chat traffic routed through the privacy filter — the paste-into-a-chatbot habit, made safe instead of banned.
When the first question about loan history arrived — the knowledge base selling itself, in the wild.
Vendor invoices staged in 90 days, each pre-coded with source attached — every one approved by a person before posting.
Reconciliation mismatches surfaced automatically before month-end — found by the system, decided by a person.
Improvement in average days-to-collect on fee invoices, from follow-ups drafted the day an invoice ages past threshold.
Automated assertions run nightly against the production configuration — plus a monthly deliberate failure drill.
Regressions caught by the harness before any staff member encountered them. Zero found by staff first.
Entries on the tamper-evident audit log — every action traceable to its trigger, its approver, and its source document.
Of the harness is generic assertion-running; the remainder is client-specific fixtures. Which means it deploys anywhere — including on AI systems somebody else built.

boundary.label: Approve
boundary.desc: The work moves forward — approved on first presentation, most within the hour.

boundary.label: Send back
boundary.desc: Returned with comments. Every send-back becomes training signal and, where it generalizes, a new test case.

boundary.label: Escalate
boundary.desc: Handed to the right person, plus every request that waited too long. Escalation is automatic; silence never means yes.
